draft.title: Levels of planning
card: covers several years and the whole business. It sets the broad direction, such as opening in a new state.
covers one to two years and a part of the business, such as the marketing team. It turns the strategic plan into steps for that part.
covers the day-to-day work, such as a weekly roster or daily orders of stock. It keeps routine tasks running.
The levels link up. Operational plans support tactical plans, and tactical plans support the strategic plan.
draft.remember: Strategic is long and whole-business. Tactical is one to two years for a part. Operational is day to day.

a.q: Which of these is an example of a strategic plan?
opts: A five-year plan to expand a bakery chain into Queensland
A plan to run a social media campaign for the next year
A roster that sets who works each shift this week
A schedule for ordering flour every Monday morning
a.why: Expanding into a new state covers several years and affects the whole business, so it is strategic. The social media campaign is tempting, but it covers one year and one part of the business, so it is tactical.
a.clue: Look for the plan with the longest time and the widest reach.

b.q: Priya manages the sales team at a furniture company in Newcastle. She writes a plan for the next 18 months to lift online sales, which supports the owner's five-year growth plan. What level of plan is Priya's?
opts: Tactical, as it covers one to two years for one part
Strategic, as it helps the owner's long-term growth goal
Operational, as it is made by a manager, not the owner
Operational, as it deals with sales that happen each day
b.why: The plan runs 18 months and covers only the sales team, so it is tactical. It is not strategic even though it supports a strategic plan, because strategic plans cover several years and the whole business.
b.clue: Check the length of time and how much of the business the plan covers.

a.best: A five-year plan to expand a bakery chain into Queensland

b.best: Tactical, as it covers one to two years for one part
